designFeedback.findingDescription: Apps like Finch use a cozy, supportive interface for tracking daily goals, making productivity feel gentle rather than demanding. Add a floating "log today" button or a prominent quick-tap region at the bottom of the daily todo list that pre-fills today's date and opens a minimal modal (rank + title only). The best habit tracking apps offer a seamless habits setup process, making sure users log habits fast, reducing friction vs. the current three-step add flow.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Streaks with Confetti Micro-Animation on Daily Mark
designFeedback.findingDescription: Subtle micro animations and visual feedback like confetti explosions reward user actions in real-time. Mission Control has a static streak counter. Add a brief 1-second confetti burst (via CSS keyframes) when a user checks off today's first/final task, triggering only on the streak badge itself. Habit trackers now commonly feature confetti animations and Android support, and retro JRPG menus pair well with particle effects.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Difficulty Signaling via Visual Layering (Bento Grid Weight)
designFeedback.findingDescription: Bento grid is an information architecture decision that controls cognitive load by giving each piece of data its own spatial weight. Apply this to daily todos: bigger/taller cards for high-rank (S/A) tasks, compact rows for routine (C) ones. This mirrors how a hero tile spanning 6 columns creates visual hierarchy through spatial weight so the bigger tile appears more important—letting users visually triage at a glance without text labels.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Immediate Visual Feedback on Task Completion
designFeedback.findingDescription: The core of the experience is the visual feedback loop. When a user marks a habit as complete, the app must acknowledge it—instantly and satisfyingly. This doesn't mean over-the-top fireworks, but a clear, immediate confirmation that their effort has been recorded. Mission Control already does this well with XP pop animations; enhancing it with a color pulse or rank-check notification (e.g., "S-rank locked" at task completion) would deepen the JRPG feel.

Streak forgiveness (freezes, grace days, pause buttons) went from premium feature to baseline expectation, driven by the fact that an unforgiving streak breaks once and then breaks forever, because the psychological cost of restarting from zero is heavier than the cost of skipping today. Mission Control could let players "freeze" one day per week without losing their XP streak, or offer a monthly streak-reset token—keeping the JRPG rank feel while staying psychologically forgiving.

thread-1786428178060-0-difficulty-signal.title: Anchor + Supporting Cell Ratio (Bento Hierarchy via Area, Not Just Label)
thread-1786428178060-0-difficulty-signal.description: Every bento has one anchor that wins on size by a clear margin, ideally twice the area of the next cell, and the anchor is where the strongest copy, most important visual, or highest-stakes interaction lives. For Mission Control's daily todos, make the S-rank task an anchor (spanning 2 grid columns + 2 rows), A-ranks as secondary cells (1 col × 1.5 rows), and C-rank routine items as minimal supporting cells (1 col × 0.8 rows). This ratio mirrors the visual hierarchy the rest of the page uses, compressed into the section—users triage instantly by spatial weight alone, with no text labels required.

thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.title: Streak Confetti Burst on Daily Completion
thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.description: When the user checks off their first task of the day, trigger a brief 1-second CSS keyframe confetti animation (3–5 particles scaling and fading upward) centered on the streak badge in the header. The effect rewards daily habit closure with instant tactile feedback, reinforcing the JRPG battle-menu aesthetic while borrowing gamification momentum from modern habit trackers. Confetti only fires once per calendar day, preventing fatigue.

thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.title: One-Tap Today Log (Norm Pattern)
thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.description: Norm is a minimal habit tracker that focuses on quick daily logging, with the home screen highlighting a few recent days for fast updates. Apply this pattern to Mission Control's daily todo list by adding a prominent card at the top with a single large tap target—"Log Today"—that instantly opens a pre-filled form with today's date and a text field for the habit/task title, skipping rank selection on first pass. This mirrors how well-designed logging tools remove friction from sharing an update—if it takes more than a minute, people just won't do it.
